transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-04-29 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 54 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan Ellis (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendez (CTO - Blue Harbor Health), Rita Chen (Lead ML Engineer), Samir Patel (Backend Lead)

Summary: quick sync on app integration POC, review of last week's test runs, discussion of SDK function/tool calls and structured output schema issues, confirm next steps and benchmarks.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, um thanks for joining. quick agenda — status from Rita on the benchmark, Priya will walk through the SDK snippets for the structured output and function calls, and then we'll go over infra/security items.
[00:18] Carlos: great, thanks Jordan. we've got Samir and I on — Rita will start, yep.
[00:24] Rita: ok so quick update on the integration test runs — we ran 5k end-to-end requests through the hosted API and then 1k through our dedicated trial. the simple summary: functional flow works, most structured outputs conform but we saw about 4% schema mismatches and ~1.2% truncated responses where the JSON got cut off mid-field.
[00:45] Priya: when you say truncated, is that at token limit or streaming cutoff?
[00:48] Rita: seems like token limit in a handful of cases — we were requesting up to 600 tokens on some calls. also a couple of times the function call wrapper returned an incorrect field name — like "patient_id" vs "patientId" — probably normalization mismatch.
[01:05] Priya: ok that's helpful. for the SDK we've got two approaches: (A) strict schema enforcement client-side where the SDK validates and retries with adjusted max_tokens, and (B) server-side guardrails where we request a strict JSON schema from the model using the structured-output param and reject anything that doesn't parse.
[01:25] Samir: we prefer client-side validation because we can't add a lot of extra RTTs on the path. what's the overhead for the SDK validation?
[01:31] Priya: negligible — it's local JSON parsing and a single retry flow. the SDK also supports streaming so you can stream tokens and reconstruct the object; in many cases streaming reduces tail latency and prevents the model from over-generating which caused truncation.
[01:48] Jordan: quick numbers Rita mentioned — can you share your p50/p95?
[01:52] Rita: sure. on the hosted path for 512-token responses p50 ~180ms, p95 ~420ms. with streaming turned on and aggressive early flush in our client we got p95 down to ~260ms. Dedicated trial was a bit better in p95 but only by ~15% at current config.
[02:14] Carlos: how about cost delta for dedicated? approximate?
[02:17] Rita: running rough estimates — dedicated commitment would lower per-token cost by ~30% for sustained throughput at our expected QPS. but setup and egress were concerns.
[02:27] Priya: on egress, we showed the VPC/private path last week — Redwood Private supports VPC peering and customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest. Jordan will share the exact network diagram and the KMS integration doc.
[02:39] Samir: we need to confirm our compliance team is ok with the HSM/KMS flow. what's the requirement from your side?
[02:45] Jordan: you can either use our managed KMS with customer-managed keys, or bring your own key material via an HSM; we'll send the architecture note.
[02:52] Rita: a couple of functional issues we observed: (1) function-call responses sometimes include extra commentary outside the JSON, like "Note: ..." before the JSON payload which breaks our parser, (2) in a few calls the tool calls to our internal scheduling service returned 502s when concurrent calls spiked.
[03:12] Priya: on (1) we recommend defining the structured output schema explicitly in the prompt + using the SDK's strict_schema flag — that instructs the runtime to prefer JSON-only responses and will surface a parse error instead of returning extraneous text. SDK snippet coming after this call.
[03:28] Priya: on tool calls, we saw rate-limiting in your internal tool — are you doing retries?
[03:33] Samir: yes, we have basic retries, but not circuit breakers; we can add backoff. curious about Redwood's best practices for tool-call timeouts and retries in high concurrency.
[03:44] Priya: we usually recommend short tool timeouts (200-500ms) and client-side concurrency limits that match the model's batching behavior. also leverage the SDK's async function-call wrapper — it batches tool calls to reduce spikes.
[03:58] Rita: can you explain that batching? we thought each user request triggers a single tool call.
[04:03] Priya: sometimes you can batch multiple low-latency lookups on the infra side; the SDK exposes a batcher that groups calls within a 10-50ms window and sends them as a single batch to the tool endpoint. this reduces upstream pressure. note: batching is workload-dependent.
[04:20] Jordan: also want to flag model selection — in our tests we used an open LLM variant that Redwood hosts; for lower latency tail and stricter output we can try a quantized variant or a different architecture — we'll propose two variants for your next benchmark.
[04:35] Carlos: any concerns about hallucinations in structured output? we've seen a couple of fields filled with default text when the tool didn't return a value.
[04:43] Priya: yep this is common. Recommended patterns: (1) explicit null-handling in schema, (2) prefer tool-first pattern where the tool returns canonical values and model only formats, (3) post-validate and if critical fields are missing, route to a fallback deterministic flow.
[05:02] Rita: on validation, we've started implementing a JSON schema validator in the service layer. the problem is sometimes the model returns slightly different keys and we end up with 4% mismatch — would prefer the model to conform rather than hard-mapping on our side.
[05:16] Priya: one trick is to use canonical examples in the prompt plus the structured-output schema field — the runtime will bias the model heavily toward the exact keys. also the SDK can optionally enforce key-level canonicalization. snippet will show this.
[05:32] Jordan: let's talk about telemetry — Rita, did you get enough traces to show token-level cost and per-route latency?
[05:39] Rita: yes we used the Redwood console trial metrics. token-level breakdown is there but we need a bit more retention for deep analysis. also would like token-attribution per route for 30 days.
[05:50] Jordan: we'll propose the console retention addon in the follow-up email.
[05:55] Carlos: on security docs — please include SOC2 timeline and audit logs granularity. our compliance team asked how deep the audit logs go and whether SAML SSO events are captured.
[06:06] Jordan: will include a SOC2 summary and the audit logs spec. Redwood captures SSO events, API keys usage, and per-call metadata at the token-level — example logs are in the doc I'll send.
[06:18] Samir: one more infra note — if we go Dedicated, can we bring our own autoscaler policies? we need to preserve burst for peak nights.
[06:25] Priya: Dedicated supports configurable autoscaling and burst capacity policies; we'll share default policies and you can submit a custom policy for review.
[06:34] Rita: what's the recommended retry pattern for function calls that mutate state? we want idempotency.
[06:39] Priya: use idempotency keys for mutating tool calls and an acknowledgement pattern. SDK provides helpers to generate and manage idempotency keys per session.
[06:49] Carlos: ok great. any blockers on the SDK side for us to proceed to a pilot ramp?
[06:54] Rita: main blocker is the schema mismatch and the parser break on extraneous text. once we get the strict_schema snippet and the streaming-enabled set up we'll re-run the benchmark.
[07:05] Priya: action: I'll push an SDK patch with strict_schema and streaming examples plus a sample batcher config. Jordan will attach the security docs and dedicated pricing.
[07:15] Jordan: cool. last thing — timeline check. are you still aiming to complete pilot acceptance in three weeks?
[07:20] Carlos: yes that's the target but depends on no new infra blockers.
[07:24] Jordan: perfect. we'll aim to get the artifacts out by Monday so you can start the next run.
[07:29] Rita: thanks, that works.
[07:31] Jordan: ok we'll recap next steps in email and close. thanks everyone.

Recap / Notes:
- SDK integration: integrated, patch for strict_schema + streaming + batcher from Priya (deliver by 2026-05-01)
- Benchmarks: customer to run 10k E2E with streaming enabled; report p50/p95 and token counts (Rita due 2026-05-06)
